sources.entry: Part-DB - Inventory management system for your electronic components. (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker/PHP/Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Part-DB is an open-source, web-based inventory management system for electronic components, installed on a web server and accessed through a browser.
summary.what_it_does: Tracks electronic parts with categories, footprints, manufacturers, storage locations, prices, tags, and attached files such as datasheets and pictures. It provides user accounts with groups and fine-grained permissions, plus two-factor authentication (Google Authenticator and WebAuthn/U2F) and optional SAML single sign-on. Projects can hold a bill of materials (BOM) that shows how many units can be built and withdraws the needed parts from inventory, and an event log records changes with the ability to revert parts to older versions. It can generate barcodes and labels, look up part data from suppliers such as Octopart, Digikey, Farnell, LCSC or TME, and offers an API, a KiCad integration, and an MCP server for AI agents.
use_cases: track a hobby electronics parts inventory
manage shared parts stock in a makerspace
build projects from stock using a bill of materials
generate barcode labels for storage locations
import part data from distributor websites
share a central parts database with KiCad
how_to_run: Copy or clone the repository onto your server and point your web server at the public/ folder
cp .env .env.local, then set APP_ENV=prod and configure DATABASE_URL if not using SQLite
php bin/console doctrine:migrations:migrate (note the generated admin password)
Access Part-DB in a browser and log in as admin; a Docker image (jbtronics/part-db1) is also available
notable: Supplier integrations that pull part information, datasheets and prices from several distributors
AI-based data extraction from shop pages and uploaded PDF datasheets
KiCad integration that exposes Part-DB parts directly inside KiCad
MCP server so AI agents can answer questions about the inventory
Browser plugin for submitting parts from any shop website
caveats: Requires a web server, PHP 8.2+, and a database server (MySQL/MariaDB or PostgreSQL) unless using SQLite; shell access is recommended
Installation is a multi-step manual process with composer and yarn builds; the README points to a separate detailed guide
Changing the database backend later is not easy and the default currency cannot be changed after prices are created
